title: Staff Software Engineer – Network Automation
description:
Why Sony Interactive Entertainment? 

Sony Interactive Entertainment isn’t just the Best Place to Play — it’s also the Best Place to Work. Sony Interactive Entertainment (SIE) is the company behind the PlayStation brand. As a subsidiary of Sony Group Corporation, we’re part of a proud legacy of innovation and excellence. SIE is a dynamic technology company, delivering cutting-edge hardware and network services to more than 100 million people and an entertainment leader, home to some of the most beloved and recognizable intellectual properties (IP) in the world. Our role at SIE is to create and nurture the experiences under the PlayStation brand, a name synonymous with entertainment excellence and creativity.

Role Overview: 

We are looking for a Staff Software Engineer to help shape and build the next generation of our network automation platforms. 

Our challenge is one of scale, complexity and criticality. We operate a massive global network supporting PlayStation Network, spanning more than 40 interconnection locations and 20+ data centres worldwide. Operating infrastructure at this scale safely and efficiently requires us to move beyond specialist-driven workflows and individual automation tools toward reliable, declarative software platforms. 

You will help make that transition. You will work on software that turns complex network and infrastructure operations into reliable, API-driven and increasingly self-service capabilities. This includes building control-plane services, declarative APIs and intent-based controllers that manage production infrastructure safely and consistently across our global footprint. 

This is a Staff-level engineering role with significant technical influence. You will combine hands-on engineering with setting technical direction: defining architectures, solving complex cross-system and distributed-systems problems, writing designs, driving alignment with senior engineers and architects, and mentoring engineers across the team. 

Your work will directly influence how one of the world's largest gaming networks is operated and automated, while establishing engineering patterns and platforms that can be reused across multiple network domains and services. 

What you'll be doing: 

- Provide technical leadership and architectural direction for network automation and infrastructure control platforms, treating the self-service network API as a product by working with users and partner teams to define outcomes, establish clear expectations for API behavior and reliability, align on team responsibilities, and ensure those commitments are met. 

- Use domain-driven design with network experts, software engineers and API consumers to establish shared language and bounded contexts, then turn those agreements into versioned, testable contracts. 

- Design and build APIs, services, controllers and reconciliation workflows that manage production infrastructure safely at scale. 

- Build on the Kubernetes API, including custom resources and control loops that continuously converge actual state toward declared intent. 

- Own the operational Kubernetes path: CRD rollout, RBAC and admission, controller health, Helm packaging, deployment drift and incident diagnosis. 

- Design distributed workflows that operate correctly under eventual consistency, at-least-once delivery, concurrent writes and partial failure, with idempotency and safe recovery as fundamental properties. 

- Design stable APIs, schemas and data models used across team boundaries, including versioning and backwards compatibility. 

- Develop patterns for multi-tenant infrastructure platforms, including tenant isolation, authorization, policy enforcement and safe automation boundaries. 

- Establish strong approaches to testing, observability and change safety for software that changes live infrastructure. 

- Improve software delivery practices through automated CI gates, versioned artifacts, controlled promotion, and safe deployment and recovery strategies. 

- Lead complex migrations and modernization of existing automation, services and data models, evaluating when components should be evolved, replaced or rewritten, and ensuring safe coexistence, behavioral compatibility and retirement of legacy paths. 

- Drive technical alignment across software engineering, networking, operations and architecture teams; lead decisions within your area of accountability, contribute constructively to decisions owned by others, and make technology choices based on long-term company and product value. 

- Mentor engineers, lead technical and design reviews, and raise software engineering standards across the wider organization. 

What we're looking for: 

Must have 

- Deep expertise in a backend language such as Python, Go, Rust or Java, including asynchronous concurrency, static typing, data modelling and validation, API development, packaging and tooling. 

- Strong experience building Kubernetes controllers or operators, including custom resources and reconciliation/control-loop patterns. 

- Strong experience building event-driven distributed systems, particularly eventual consistency, at-least-once delivery, idempotency, optimistic concurrency and partial-failure handling. 

- Experience designing and building self-service, multi-tenant platforms, including tenant isolation, policy and access control. 

- Strong API and schema design skills, including versioning and schema evolution for interfaces consumed by other teams and systems. 

- Demonstrated technical leadership across team boundaries, including driving architectural designs, building agreement among senior technical stakeholders and mentoring other engineers. 

- A track record of taking ambiguous, technically complex problems from architecture through to reliable production systems that manage large-scale infrastructure, such as networks, compute or cloud resources. 

Nice to have 

- Networking fundamentals, particularly BGP, IP fabrics and VXLAN/EVPN/L3VPN. 

- Working knowledge of Go, sufficient to understand and contribute to adjacent services and controllers. 

- Experience designing testing and observability strategies for production infrastructure automation, including systems and backends that cannot be fully reproduced in CI. 

- Experience with graph databases, or with source-of-truth systems that model infrastructure and its relationships. 

The impact 

You will help establish the architecture and engineering practices behind a new generation of network automation, moving from individual scripts and specialist-driven workflows toward declarative, model-driven and reliable platforms. 

At Staff level, your impact is expected to extend beyond the code you personally deliver. You will help shape the APIs and designs other teams build on, develop other engineers, and establish technical patterns that can be reused across multiple network domains and services.

Please refer to our Candidate Privacy Notice for more information about what personal information we collect, how we use it, who we share it with, and your data protection rights.

title: Technical Product Owner
description:
🏢 Who we are

A team from Germany with the vision to make advanced network security accessible for everyone

We are a software company developing a zero-trust network security platform that is both easy to use and affordable for teams of all sizes and budgets. Our mission is grounded in a simple yet powerful belief: secure private networking is a fundamental right of every modern company.

Since our launch on GitHub in 2021, we have gained trust among thousands of companies seeking secure and seamless solutions for connecting remote employees and infrastructure. By replacing traditional centralized VPNs, NetBird has become a trusted choice for modern network security, connecting today hundreds of thousands of users and machines worldwide. Our open-source, community-driven approach has been a key driver of our success. We listen to our users, and their input helps us make network security better for everyone.

Want to see what we're working on? Check out our GitHub repo at https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird or https://netbird.io/knowledge-hub 

✏️ What you will do 

As a Technical Product Owner at NetBird, you'll be the link between our users and our engineering team on the core NetBird platform. That means the clients, the dashboard and API, and the self-hosted setup. Today our CTO covers product next to running engineering, and you'll take over a big part of the day to day. You keep the backlog in Linear in good shape, turn feedback from customers and the community into clear, well-scoped work and make sure engineers can spend their time building. You'll report to our CTO and work closely with engineering, support and sales.

You will:

- Own the day-to-day backlog in Linear. Triage incoming issues, write clear tickets with context and acceptance criteria and keep priorities current.

- Build a simple system for collecting feedback from customers, GitHub issues, community channels, support and sales calls, and turn it into well-framed problems the team can act on.

- Talk to users and customers directly to understand their setups and the problem behind each request.

- Plan our regular cycles with engineering, break bigger features into shippable pieces, and follow them through to release.

- Keep the rest of the company in the loop on what's shipping, from release notes and changelogs to updates for sales and support.

- Close the loop with the people who gave feedback, so they know what happened with it.

- Spot patterns across feedback and bring them into roadmap discussions, backed by data where you can.

This is a technical product owner role. You won't write production code, but unlike a classic product owner you'll go deep with engineers on how things work, reproduce issues yourself and judge how much effort a request really takes. It's also a hands-on role in a small team. There's no big product org around you yet, so you'll help shape how product work runs at NetBird as we grow.

🔎 What we are looking for 

We're looking for someone who is at home in technical conversations, both with our engineers and with our users, who mostly work in IT and infrastructure teams. You also like structure and keep a busy backlog in order.

Must-Haves 

- 3+ years of experience as a Product Owner, Product Manager, or in a similar role at a (technical) B2B SaaS, infrastructure, or developer tools company.

- A technical background. You're comfortable reading API docs, following a GitHub discussion, and digging into how something works together with engineers.

- Understanding of networking basics like IP, DNS, routing, firewalls, and VPNs.

- Hands-on experience running a backlog in Linear, Jira, or similar, and writing tickets engineers can pick up without a follow-up meeting.

- Experience working directly with customers or users and turning their feedback into prioritized work.

- Good judgment on priorities. You can say no, explain why, and keep people aligned.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills in English. You default to writing things down.

- You work AI native. You use AI tools and coding agents every day, for example to sort feedback, dig into a problem or draft tickets, and you know where they help and where they don't.

- Comfortable in a small, fast-moving team where processes are still being built.

Nice-to-Haves 

- Experience with networking, security, or zero trust products.

- Experience with open source projects or developer communities.

- Experience building CLI products.

- Hands-on experience with self-hosting, Docker, Kubernetes, or cloud infrastructure.

- Some coding experience, enough to read a PR or reproduce a bug yourself.

- Experience using product analytics to back up decisions.

😌 What’s in it for you 

We want you to do meaningful work and be proud of what you build.

That’s why we offer:

- Comprehensive compensation package : Receive a competitive base salary and equity incentives.

- Hybrid work environment : Enjoy the flexibility of working both from our centrally located Berlin office and remotely.

- Real product ownership: A direct say in what our engineering team builds next.

- Open source impact: Work in the open on a popular open source project, in direct contact with our customers and community.

- Growth opportunities : The chance to build up our product team from the start, with room to grow as NetBird scales.

If you don't tick every box, apply anyway. And if you have time, try NetBird first and tell us in your application one thing you'd change.

title: Staff Backend Engineer - Search Features & APIs (SABR)
description:
About us

Launched in 2019, Constructor is an AI-first e-commerce search and discovery platform that helps shoppers find the right products at the right time and enables leading global e-commerce brands to drive meaningful revenue and conversion gains.

About the team

The SABR team owns the top layer of request processing for product discovery. We own the service that first receives product discovery requests (autocomplete, search, browse & recommendations) & executes the entire business logic that drives product discovery. That service also functions as a gateway to parse incoming user requests, orchestrate calls across the internal services that do the ranking and retrieval, interpret their responses, and assemble the final response the customer sees. We also own the public configuration APIs customers use to control how discovery behaves, and the MCP layer that exposes all of it to AI agents.

Our team owns both platform & product components: Because of the positioning of our services, we take part in every architectural decision of our core product offering. At the same time, our goals are heavily influenced by direct customer feedback, because all product discovery-related features are either implemented in or integrated with our services.

All of our services are public APIs, so interface design and backward compatibility are a constant part of the job. But most of our attention goes to keeping them fast and up: we serve up to 15k RPS, fan out to many internal services on every request, and are expected to stay available and degrade gracefully when any of them fails or slows down.

The work is distributed systems in practice rather than in theory: request orchestration, failure isolation, caching, latency budgets, capacity planning, and the observability to know what is actually happening in production. The team is small enough that engineers own problems end to end, from design through on-call.

About you

You're a staff-level engineer who wants to own systems, not tickets. You've built high-traffic, low-latency Python services and carried the pager for them. You think in trade-offs: latency versus cost, flexibility versus a public API that customers can't afford to see break, the fix that ships this week versus the architecture that has to last two years. You can lead work that spans several engineers and several quarters, you enjoy mentoring others, and you're fine when a problem shows up half-defined. You don't mind being the one who reads the spec for some unfamiliar protocol, works out how it fits, and designs an integration that holds up at scale. You change your mind when someone has a better argument, you make the people around you better, and you still care about your code long after it merges.

What you will do

- Own the technical direction of one or more of our services - architecture, performance, and reliability.

- Lead design of new systems and public APIs, and the evolution of existing ones as traffic and feature scope grow.

- Raise the engineering bar through design and code review, and mentor mid and senior engineers into owning bigger scopes.

- Partner with product, other engineering teams, and solutions/support to shape what we build and to represent search constraints and trade-offs honestly.

- Take part in on-call for the systems you own, and lead incident response and follow-through when things break.

What we are looking for

Technical

- Substantial experience building and operating high-traffic, low-latency backend services in production.

- Extensive Python knowledge (our primary language).

- Experience with observability and performance work in live systems.

- Experience designing and evolving public APIs that external customers depend on.

- Experience designing & implementing scalable service-oriented architectures.

Beyond the code

- Track record of leading projects that span multiple engineers and quarters.

- Influence without authority, and willingness to change your position when someone has a better argument.

- Clear written communication - design docs, RFCs, postmortems.

- Good judgment about trade-offs and scope.

- Comfort with ambiguity and loosely defined problems.

- Ownership that extends past merge, to how the system behaves in production.

Nice to have

- Experience with AWS

- Background in search, ranking, information retrieval, or e-commerce product discovery.

- Exposure to AI/LLM-facing infrastructure (MCP, agent tooling, or similar).

Du verbindest Strategie mit täglicher Umsetzung: die richtigen Zielgruppen identifizieren, starke Ansprache entwickeln, Menschen besser machen und aus guten Gesprächen verlässlich neue Sales-Chancen schaffen. Dabei gehst du selbst ans Telefon, testest neue Ansätze und setzt den Standard für dein Team. Dich erwarten hohes Tempo, viel Gestaltungsspielraum und direkte Verantwortung für unser Wachstum.

Standort: Berlin
- Outbound-Pipeline verantworten: Du verantwortest den Aufbau und die Weiterentwicklung unserer Outbound-Pipeline – von der Auswahl passender Accounts über die Erstansprache bis zur qualifizierten Übergabe an unser Sales Team.
- Selbst vorangehen: Du bist als Player-Coach aktiv in der Akquise. Du führst selbst Cold Calls, testest Gesprächseinstiege und Einwandbehandlung und zeigst deinem Team, wie aus einem ersten Kontakt eine echte Sales-Chance wird.
- Outbound-Strategie entwickeln: Du legst fest, welche Zielgruppen wir mit welchen Botschaften über welche Kanäle erreichen. Cold Calling ist der Kern, ergänzt durch weitere Kontaktpunkte wie LinkedIn, E-Mail und Messen.
- Neue ICPs und Personas erschließen: Gemeinsam mit unserem GTM-Team entwickelst und validierst du neue ideale Kundenprofile und Buyer Personas. Du priorisierst Segmente und findest heraus, wo wir wiederholbar qualifizierte Pipeline aufbauen können.
- Prozesse und Playbooks aufbauen: Du entwickelst klare Standards für Recherche, Ansprache, Follow-ups, Qualifizierung und Übergabe. Erfolgreiche Ansätze übersetzt du in Playbooks, die das gesamte Team im Alltag nutzen kann.
- Performance steuern: Du definierst gemeinsam mit Sales klare Ziele und steuerst das Team anhand relevanter Kennzahlen – von erreichten Entscheidern und qualifizierten Terminen bis zu akzeptierten Sales-Chancen und generierter Pipeline. Du erkennst Engpässe und leitest konkrete Verbesserungen ab.
- Tools und Daten nutzbar machen: Du sorgst für saubere CRM-Daten, transparente Reports und einen sinnvollen Einsatz unserer Sales-Tools. Dein Team soll seine Zeit in gute Gespräche investieren können.
- Hiring und Onboarding mitgestalten: Du hilfst uns, weitere Talente zu gewinnen, und entwickelst ein strukturiertes Onboarding, mit dem neue Teammitglieder schnell produktiv werden.
- Eng mit GTM, Sales und Produkt arbeiten: Du stellst sicher, dass aus dem Feedback deiner Gespräche bessere Botschaften, eine präzisere Positionierung und wertvolle Impulse für unsere Software entstehen.

Das bringst du mit - Du bringst mehrjährige Erfahrung im B2B-Outbound-Vertrieb mit, idealerweise in einem SaaS- oder Technologieunternehmen, und hast nachweislich qualifizierte Pipeline aufgebaut.
- Du hast bereits ein SDR-, BDR- oder Outbound-Team geführt oder als Senior im Team konkrete Verantwortung für Coaching, Onboarding und gemeinsame Ergebnisse übernommen.
- Du beherrschst Cold Calling aus eigener Praxis. Du kannst gute Gespräche selbst führen und anderen verständlich vermitteln, was sie erfolgreich macht.
- Du weißt, wie man aus einzelnen erfolgreichen Vertriebsaktivitäten einen verlässlichen Prozess entwickelt – mit klaren Zielgruppen, relevanter Ansprache und konsequenten Follow-ups.
- Du kannst Leistung einfordern und Menschen dabei unterstützen, sie zu erreichen. Du gibst direktes, konstruktives Feedback und schaffst ein Umfeld, in dem dein Team Verantwortung übernimmt.
- Du arbeitest strukturiert und datenbasiert. Du erkennst, ob ein Engpass bei der Aktivität, Erreichbarkeit, Gesprächsqualität oder Qualifizierung liegt, und setzt dort an.
- Du fühlst dich in einem schnell wachsenden Startup wohl, triffst Entscheidungen und bringst neue Ideen zügig in die Umsetzung.
- Du gehst sicher mit HubSpot oder einem vergleichbaren CRM um und hast Erfahrung mit gängigen Outbound- und Lead-Generation-Tools.
- Du begeisterst dich für die Transformation der Energiebranche und möchtest mit deinem Team innovative Software im Handwerk etablieren.
- Du sprichst fließend Deutsch.

Was wir bieten - Wachse mit uns: Als Teil eines schnell wachsenden, YC-backed Climate-Tech-Startup mit einem ambitionierten Team.
- Echte Verantwortung: Von der ersten Idee bis zum Endergebnis, du gestaltest aktiv mit.
- Wenig Ego, viel Vertrauen: No-Blame Culture, offenes Feedback, Zusammenarbeit statt Hierarchie.
- Sei Teil der Energiewende: Mit deiner Arbeit treibst du täglich den Umstieg auf Wärmepumpen und Solar voran.
- Hybrid in Berlin-Mitte: 3 Tage gemeinsam in unserem Büro am Weinbergspark, 2 Tage Homeoffice. Mehr Flexibilität nötig? Wir finden eine Lösung.
- Modernes Equipment: MacBook und 27″-Monitor.
- Jährliches Team Retreat und regelmäßige Team-Events.
- Mobilität: Dance E-Bike oder Deutschland-Ticket.
- Fitness: Mitgliedschaft im Urban Sports Club.

Next steps - Bewirb dich online mit einem aussagekräftigen Lebenslauf.
- Dein Ansprechpartner ist Philipp Hulm (Sales Lead).
- Nach dem Screening erhältst Du von uns Bescheid, ob wir gemeinsam mit Dir den nächsten Schritt gehen möchten.
- Im ersten Schritt führen wir mit Dir ein ca. 30-minütiges Google-Meet-Interview mit einer Person aus unserem Sales Team.
- Im zweiten Schritt führen wir mit Dir ein weiteres ca. 30-minütiges Google-Meet-Interview mit unserem Gründer Thies.
- Danach laden wir Dich zu einem Face-2-Face Interview in unser Berliner Büro ein.

title: Working student (all genders) - Talent Development
description:
Become part of our mission With high-end software engineering, we inspire our customers every day through digital transformation projects. What makes the decisive difference in our success? Our XITASOnians - the people who go above and beyond every day. As part of our agile talent development , we ensure that every individual at XITASO can reach their full potential right from the start.

During your working student position , you’ll have the opportunity to help shape agile talent development up close - from supporting our mentoring system to employee satisfaction and exciting future topics such as the use of AI in talent development . We look forward to seeing the impact you’ll make through a variety of operational and conceptual tasks!

We’re interested in a long-term collaboration and are flexible in structuring the working student position. The expected number of hours is 20 hours per week . 

These tasks interest you - You’ll provide support across various areas of talent development, such as the design of new development formats or the further enhancement of our agile feedback structures .
- You’ll contribute to the continuous optimization of our internal mentoring system and play an active role in the co-creation of various mentoring formats and tools.
- You’ll take responsibility for the area of employee satisfaction as your own project - from preparation and regular execution to deriving concrete actions from our employee satisfaction survey, as well as ensuring its continuous improvement and valid foundation.
- You’ll assist with operational tasks in talent development, such as organizational tasks in preparing training events or maintaining data.
- Together with us, you’ll explore how AI can facilitate and enrich our agile talent development .
- You’ll take on research tasks and in-depth analyses , such as cross-comparisons of mentoring concepts in other agile organizations, human empowerment in dealing with complexity and ambiguity, and motivation and empowerment outside of hierarchical structures.

That makes you stand out - You are studying (Business) Psychology or HR Management or are pursuing a comparable degree program - in the second half of your bachelor’s program or in your master’s program.
- You have already gained some professional experience in the field of HR , ideally in Talent Development .
- You enjoy familiarizing yourself with new, complex topics, such as agile talent development or lateral leadership. 
- You’re excited to learn new tools and have an affinity for and openness to working with AI . 
- You’re an excellent team player and stand out for your enthusiasm, proactivity, and ability to work independently .
- You are open to serving as a workshop facilitator on a long-term basis or speaking internally on talent development topics.
- You possess very strong communication skills and can perform your role in German and English (at least C1 level in each language).

What we offer you New Work & Culture - Self-organized teams with plenty of creative freedom
- Responsibility and the opportunity to shape the work
- An open culture of learning from mistakes and giving feedback
Mentoring & Personal Development - Individual mentoring from day one
- Regular development reviews (catch-ups)
- Leadership on a equal footing, based on trust and respect
Lifelong Learning - Technical and cross-functional training
- Internal TechTalks, external training courses, and conferences
High-End Software Engineering - Challenging, innovative, and diverse projects
- Cross-functional teams using modern technologies
- A culture of expertise and cross-team knowledge sharing
Family-Friendly Environment - Subsidy for childcare costs of up to 250 € per child
- Continued pay for days when children are sick
Community & Events - Regular events (e.g., retreats, summer festivals)
- Personal interactions & team cohesion
- Part of a diverse, connected community from Day 1
Work Hours & Flexibility - Freedom to choose work hours and location
- Flexible work time accounts, 30 days of vacation, part-time option, sabbatical & workation 
Health & Well-being - Mental Health Task Force
- JobRad & other benefits
Diversity & Inclusion - Diversity Task Force for a diversity of perspectives
- Culture of belonging: Everyone should feel accepted

Salary information Within our standardized and transparent salary framework, the pay for this position ranges from €15.50 to €19.50 per hour and is based on various factors, such as qualifications and experience.

title: Software Engineer – Internal Tools & Automation (m/w/d)
description:
Gemeinsam großartig – werde Teil des Teams Du willst als Software Engineer mit Python , APIs und Automatisierungen an Lösungen arbeiten, die direkt im operativen Alltag eingesetzt werden? In dieser Rolle entwickelst du interne Tools, Services und Schnittstellen, übersetzt Anforderungen aus den Fachbereichen in pragmatische technische Lösungen und verbindest bestehende Systeme sinnvoll miteinander. Dabei arbeitest du mit modernen Webtechnologien, Datenbanken und API-basierten Integrationen und entwickelst deine Lösungen von ersten Prototypen und MVPs Schritt für Schritt zu stabilen, wartbaren Anwendungen weiter.

Deine Mission - Du entwickelst neue und bestehende interne Anwendungen und Services mit Python weiter und setzt konkrete Anforderungen aus unserem operativen Geschäft technisch um.
- Du arbeitest gemeinsam mit unseren Fachbereichen daran, Business-Anforderungen zu verstehen, zu strukturieren und daraus pragmatische technische Lösungsansätze, Prototypen und MVPs zu entwickeln.
- Du erkennst gemeinsam mit dem Team Automatisierungs- und Optimierungspotenziale und verbindest bestehende Systeme über APIs, Datenbanken und Schnittstellen.
- Du entwickelst funktionierende Prototypen zu stabilen und wartbaren Lösungen weiter und bekommst bei Architekturfragen sowie der Integration in zentrale Systeme Unterstützung und Sparring aus unserem technischen Team und dem Core Platform Team.
- Du sorgst mit sauberem und testbarem Code, automatisierten Tests und verständlicher technischer Dokumentation für die Qualität deiner Lösungen und nutzt moderne AI-Tools dort, wo sie deine Arbeit sinnvoll unterstützen.

Deine Talente - Du hast bereits praktische Erfahrung in der Softwareentwicklung gesammelt und eigenständig an Anwendungen, Tools oder Automatisierungen gearbeitet. Gute Kenntnisse in Python und/oder JavaScript beziehungsweise TypeScript bringst du bereits mit.
- Du hast ein gutes Grundverständnis von APIs, Datenbanken und grundlegenden Software-Architekturen und hast bereits mit Git sowie kollaborativen Entwicklungsprozessen gearbeitet.
- Du kennst die Grundlagen von sauberem, wartbarem und testbarem Code und hast idealerweise bereits erste Berührungspunkte mit CI/CD, automatisierten Tests oder Docker. Du musst darin noch kein Profi sein.
- Du denkst gerne über die reine technische Umsetzung hinaus, interessierst dich für den Business-Kontext und hast Lust, Anforderungen gemeinsam mit technischen und nicht-technischen Stakeholdern weiterzuentwickeln. Gleichzeitig bist du neugierig, lernbereit und offen für Feedback.
- Du nutzt AI-Tools wie ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor oder vergleichbare Anwendungen bereits im Entwicklungsalltag oder möchtest dich stärker damit beschäftigen und lernen, sie sinnvoll und verantwortungsvoll einzusetzen.
- Du verfügst über Deutschkenntnisse auf mindestens B2-Niveau für die Zusammenarbeit mit unseren Fachbereichen sowie Englischkenntnisse auf mindestens C1-Niveau für technische Dokumentation, Tools und Code.

Tech Stack 
Python | FastAPI | Docker | CI/CD | Git | SQL

Unser Angebot - #HybridFlex: Passe deine Arbeitszeiten an deine Produktivität an und arbeite mit unserem Hybrid-Work-Modell flexibel von zu Hause oder unseren zentralen Offices. Wir geben dir den Raum, den du brauchst.
- #YourTech2Shine: Mac oder Windows? Du entscheidest. Dazu liefern wir dir die passende Home-Office-Ausstattung für maximale Produktivität.
- #StarkesDuGesundesWir: Von JobRad und Hansefit-Mitgliedschaft bis zu (Online-) Gesundheitstagen und physiotherapeutischen Massagen vor Ort, ergonomisch ausgestatteten Büros, Betriebsärztin, Vertrauensperson und umfangreichem betrieblichem Gesundheitsmanagement – wir fördern aktiv deine Gesundheit und dein Wohlbefinden.
- #Ausgewogenheit: 30 Tage Urlaub, Zeiterfassung mit Überstundenausgleich – selbstverständlich. Mit zahlreichen Sportgeräten im Office, Fitness- und Coffee-Breaks oder auch Corporate Benefits für mehr Spaß beim Shoppen setzen wir Ansätze für regenerative Pausen. Zeit ist ein Investment. In dich und uns.
- #Gestaltungsmöglichkeiten: Je nach deinen Interessen und Stärken kannst du deine Expertise in spannende Projekte einbringen und gemeinsam mit WattFox unser Wachstum und unseren Erfolg mitgestalten.
- #AnkommenUndLoslegen: Wir legen Wert auf eine strukturierte Einarbeitung. Daher geben wir dir sowohl kulturell als auch fachlich alles mit, damit du dich bestmöglich entwickeln kannst.
- #GemeinsamGroßartig: Als kununu Top Company 2026 stehen bei uns Erfolg, Teamgeist und Spaß im Vordergrund. Bleib durch unsere unternehmensweiten Jourfixe am Ball und erlebe Sommerfeste, Weihnachtsfeiern, Stammtische und viele Events mehr, die unser Wir-Gefühl stärken.

Wer wir sind Seit 2011 vom Start-up zum grünen Marktführer! Jeden Monat unterstützen wir mehrere zehntausend Menschen dabei, nachhaltige Energielösungen zu finden und einfach richtige Entscheidungen zu treffen. Wir gehen die Hürde zwischen Verbrauchenden und Anbietenden mit unseren Online-Angebotsvergleichen an, ermitteln die individuellen Bedürfnisse der Anfragenden und bringen sie mit den passenden Anbietenden zusammen – ein Win-Win für alle.

title: Legal AI Engineer (Berlin or Leipzig)
description:
Description Legartis is on a mission: to unlock legal work at scale.

We set the standard for AI-powered contract work by offering a platform that changes how legal teams work, from drafting through negotiation to completion. We are now looking for the person who turns what customers actually need into what our AI actually does.

Joining Legartis is not taking a job, you take ownership. We are a team of product builders and lawyers, who do not chase hype; we build substance. If you are a lawyer who builds, someone who has stopped waiting for better tools and started making them, this is your moment and your place.

Send us your CV, a short note on why Legartis, and links to anything you have built or published.

Your mission Most companies split this seat across three teams, and that split is exactly the problem. The person who hears the customer describe their workflow should be the person who writes the requirement, and the person who writes the requirement should be able to build the first version themselves. That is you.

1. You translate customer reality into engineering requirements — and into revenue. You sit in customer and expert calls alongside Sales, not as a note-taker but as the person who understands the legal work. In trials and hackathons you coach hands-on: the customer drives, you navigate, and they create the first "wow" moment themselves. When they say "that won't work for us" or "we'll build it ourselves", you answer with a concrete path (a workaround, a workflow, the honest maintenance cost of the alternative) and you leave every conversation with a next step: trial licenses, a hackathon, a scoped rollout. Then you pull out the workflow: what actually happens, in what order, where it breaks, what the customer would pay to never do again. And you write the spec, edge cases, and acceptance criteria that Engineering can build against.

2. You build the skills yourself. You write, test, and ship agent skills and playbooks that solve real customer workflows. You build the evaluation frameworks and test sets that prove they got better rather than just different. When the AI fails on a clause, you diagnose why, at the prompt and context level, and you either fix it or hand Engineering a diagnosis precise enough to act on.

3. You make it repeatable, and therefore sellable. Anything you build once for one customer, you turn into something Sales and Customer Success can run without you. Standard demo environments. A skill library they can reach for. Onboarding that lands in days rather than months. Where Customer Success needs legal depth you step in, fix it, and turn the fix into something the team can handle alone next time. Your success is measured by how rarely you need to be in the room, and by what happens to adoption and expansion when you are not.

4. You are the legal authority in the building. Legal and compliance questions land with you: contract reviews, customer security and data protection questions, the occasional in-house matter which makes roughly ten to fifteen percent of your time. You use our own product to do it, and you tell us honestly when it is not good enough.

Your profile The person we picture. There is a name emerging for what we are describing, and it is not "lawyer who is good with computers". It is legal quant : a lawyer who builds their own tooling to practise law, rather than waiting for a vendor to ship it. The distinction that matters to us: plenty of lawyers now use AI. A legal quant builds with it. They look at a workflow and ask how to redesign it from first principles to get the best possible outcome, rather than making the existing process incrementally faster.

A note on how we are weighting this role. Three capabilities make someone exceptional here: commercial instinct, legal depth, and technical ability to build. The ideal candidate has all three. We know that person is rare, and we are not going to pretend otherwise by writing a wish list and hoping. So for this role we weight the technical evidence most heavily, because it is the hardest of the three to teach on the job.

If you believe you genuinely combine all three, we want to talk to you regardless of how neatly your CV matches the bullets below. Say so in your note and tell us what you have built and what you have sold.

1. Technical track record. You have built things and they exist and ideally you have published some of it. You are fluent with LLMs the way a practitioner is fluent, not a spectator: you know how context windows fail you or why a prompt stopped working. When something breaks you go into the system rather than around it. Scripting, Git, and APIs are a strong plus.

2. Legal foundation. A law degree with a commercial-contracts focus: German-qualified (Bachelor, Master, or Staatsexamen) or an equivalent qualification from another jurisdiction. No bar admission required, no second Staatsexamen required. What we need: you have worked hands-on with German commercial contracts, drafting, reviewing, and negotiating them, and you can hold a conversation with a General Counsel as a peer.

3. Commercial and entrepreneurial track record. You have carried commercial responsibility for something of your own: a freelance client base, a legal tech product, or a company you started. You know what it takes to win a client from a standing start and why "they did not understand the value" is never the customer's fault. If instead you have supported enterprise sales teams in demos, pilots, and expert calls, tell us what you changed about the outcome.

You prioritise by impact, you are comfortable deciding without permission, and you would rather ship something imperfect this week than something elegant next quarter.

4. Language. Excellent German and English. German is non-negotiable: our customers are DACH legal teams and the nuance lives in their language. You can run a room of legal buyers, ask the sharp question, and write a specification precise enough to build from. Other EU languages are a plus.

Why us? - Impact over hype. You define a new discipline at the intersection of law, product, and AI. Your work directly shapes how thousands of legal professionals will operate.
- No silos. You sit between Product, Engineering, and the customer, with a direct line to all three. The better argument wins, not the higher title.
- We invest in you. The enterprise motion (multi-stakeholder pilots, procurement cycles, security reviews) is teachable, and we teach it: side by side in real customer calls from week one.
- Real ownership. Competitive salary and employee stock options (ESOP).
- Build in public. We want you to keep publishing what you build, because it makes you better and it makes us visible.
- Offices in Berlin, Leipzig, and Zurich with a flexible hybrid setup. Regular apéros, lunches, and hiking trips as we enjoy the journey together.

Process - Expectations. A conversation with the People Manager about the role and who you are.
- Depth. A conversation with our General Counsel & Head of Legal AI on Legal Engineering at Legartis and where the legal market is going.
- Build session. A live case at the intersection of legal reasoning, prompting, and product work: a real customer scenario, a legal AI workflow, or a playbook that misbehaves.
- Meet the team in Leipzig or Berlin.
- A mutual decision, before we welcome you to the team.

Your mission At Wandelbots, we are building NOVA, a platform that makes industrial robot programming accessible to everyone. Our Simulation team develops the technologies that allow partners, customers, and internal teams to work with photorealistic digital twins of real production environments.

The first step is internal standardization. We want to replace individually maintained environments and hand-crafted deployments with one reproducible, documented solution that teams can use independently: scene in, session out, without requiring the Simulation team to operate every setup. You will join the Simulation team and focus on the infrastructure and operational foundations of these systems. You will not be building them in isolation: Wandelbots has an established infrastructure team responsible for shared infrastructure and platform capabilities. You will work closely with that team while owning the simulation-specific workloads, deployment patterns, and operational requirements.

description:

About the Role 

We are seeking a commercially minded Senior Manager to join Volta's tax function and lead delivery on deals, structuring, and modelling. This role would suit someone looking to move in-house at a fast-scaling, capital-intensive platform.

Reporting to the VP of Tax, this is a hands-on delivery role. The Senior Manager will lead deal workstreams, build and stress-test tax models, and monitor governance to ensure tax structures are operating as intended with genuine scope for the remit to grow as the function and business scale.

Key Responsibilities 

Deal Execution & Structuring 

- Lead the day-to-day tax workstream on live transactions - fundraising and capital raises, infrastructure investments and acquisitions, joint ventures, financing and refinancing.

- Coordinate tax due diligence, documentation and completion mechanics with Finance, Capital Markets, Corporate Development, Legal and external advisers.

Tax Modelling & Commercial Analysis 

- Own the build and maintenance of tax models and supporting schedules for investments, financing structures and transactions.

- Model cash-tax outcomes and sensitivities, including:

- Tax depreciation and capital allowances

- Interest deductibility and financing scenarios

- Loss utilisation and group relief

- Withholding taxes, repatriation and transfer-pricing charges

- VAT and other indirect-tax cash flows

- Restructuring, refinancing and exit scenarios

- Feed agreed tax assumptions into the wider financial models, working closely with Finance and Capital Markets.

- Pressure-test tax assumptions prepared by internal teams and advisers for technical accuracy and consistency.

- Translate the tax impact into terms deal teams can use directly – cash flow, valuation and investor returns.

International Tax

- Flag material international tax developments relevant to live deals or models.

- Help operate Volta's tax governance framework and controls on a day-to-day basis and keep the tax risk register current.

- Build and maintain supporting documentation for tax positions, transactions and intercompany arrangements.

- Manage the working relationship with Big Four and legal advisers on live matters, escalating scope, cost or quality issues.

- Support tax authority enquiries, audits and ruling applications.

Business Partnering 

- Act as the day-to-day tax contact for Finance, Legal, Capital Markets, Corporate Development and Strategy on live workstreams.

- Give practical, timely tax input on new projects and initiatives, translated into cash flow, returns and capital-efficiency impact.

- Prepare materials and analysis for the VP of Tax ahead of CFO, leadership, investor and lender conversations.

- Take ownership of agreed workstreams end-to-end, escalating judgement calls and anything strategically significant to the VP of Tax.

Process & Team Support 

- Help the VP of Tax roll out new processes, controls and systems as the function scales.

- Manage or mentor junior tax analyst/associates as the team grows.

- Identify opportunities for automation and standardisation in day-to-day tax processes and modelling.

Experience & Qualifications 

- Strong relevant tax experience, typically Big Four Senior Manager to Associate Director level, or the in-house equivalent – someone used to executing complex cross-border deals rather than only advising on them.

- Professional qualification: CTA, ACA, CA or equivalent.

- Hands-on experience structuring cross-border investments and financing.

- Solid technical grounding in international corporate tax – transfer pricing, withholding taxes, permanent establishment and tax-treaty matters.

- Proven tax-modelling ability, comfortable translating technical rules into cash-flow, valuation and investor-return outputs.

- Experience coordinating multi-jurisdiction compliance and external advisers.

Skills & Attributes 

- Execution-focused and detail-oriented, with good judgement about what to escalate and when.

- Comfortable owning a workstream end-to-end while operating within a strategy set by someone else.

- Strong project-management skills, coordinating multiple internal and external stakeholders at once.

- A clear communicator, able to explain complex tax positions to non-tax audiences.

- Pragmatic and collaborative, energised by building good process in a fast-moving environment.

Desirable Experience 

- Background in private equity, infrastructure funds, real assets, energy or digital infrastructure.

- Time in a start-up or rapidly scaling international organisation.

- Exposure to data centres or other capital-intensive infrastructure businesses.

- Familiarity with UK, European and US tax environments.

- Experience with tax accounting, provisions and cash-tax forecasting.

REQ-167

As a global team, we do our best to provide great benefits wherever you're based. While some benefits vary by country due to local regulations, we believe looking after our people is simply the right thing to do.

Design engineers sit at the intersection of design and engineering. As a design engineer at WRITER, you'll own the Writer Design System (WDS) — how it's built, how it's maintained, and how both humans and AI agents use it to ship product.

This role matters more now than ever. AI coding agents write more of our production code, and they ship whatever they find. A design system that's incomplete or inconsistent doesn't just slow designers down; it gets compounded at scale by every agent that builds against it. You'll make sure WRITER's core UI library is complete and trustworthy enough to build on, working closely with the designers, PMs, and engineers who rely on it every day. - Own the Writer Design System (WDS) as your primary domain — agentify and maintain it, ensuring it's optimized for both humans and AI agents building with it

- Design and build production-quality UI components and features, owning surfaces from sketch to ship

- Ship design-led work that wouldn't survive an engineering backlog — polish passes, micro-interactions, and brand moments that make the product feel alive

- Architect new primitives and extend the system's core components, shaping its technical direction while keeping documentation, examples, and libraries in sync across Figma, .md skills, and Storybook

- Help shape the design-to-code workflow, researching the latest tools and practices to unlock org-wide productivity and democratize workflows across the EPD organization

- 4–8+ years building production frontends with TypeScript and React, with a track record of owning a system, platform, or surface end-to-end rather than individual features

- Solid instincts for animation principles including easing curves, choreography, anticipation, follow-through, interruptibility, and perceived performance

- Fluency in Figma at expert level — auto-layout, variants, variables, and code connect — and proficiency with design engineering technologies like framer-motion, gsap, and lottie for web-based animation

- Experience driving adoption of a design system or shared platform across an engineering org, with a track record of influencing technical or design direction beyond your immediate team

- Experience with AI product surfaces — tool-call UIs, streaming responses, agent state, and dynamic UI rendering — and comfort navigating ambiguous, cross-team problems with good judgment about when to loop others in

- A genuine commitment to WRITER's values of Connect, Challenge, and Own

POSITION DESCRIPTION 

This is not a traditional sales engineering role. As a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE), you are at the critical intersection of our code, our clients, and their most critical missions. You will be deployed to our most strategic partners, embedding within their environments to solve high-stakes problems that have no textbook answers.

You own the "last mile" of our product's impact , ensuring our technology fundamentally transforms how our users confront challenges such as financial crime, supply chain disruption, and threats to national security.

You are equal parts engineer, strategist, and operator. One day you might be architecting a data pipeline within a client's cloud environment ; the next, you'll be writing production Python to integrate our API into a proprietary analytics platform ; and by the end of the week, you could be briefing a C-level executive, intelligence analyst, or mission director on the outcomes your work has enabled.

title: Global Hub Operations Director
description:
About WPP Production 

We are WPP Production - the unified global production company that brings together all of WPP's content producers, studios and craft experts into one connected organisation. We combine world-class human craft with next generation technology to originate, design, and deliver multi-channel content systems at scale. Built for borderless collaboration and powered by deep craft expertise, we are the production engine designed for today's always on, AI driven marketing world.

About WPP 

WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world's leading brands. We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. For more information, visit WPP.com .

A Hybrid working model 

We believe the best work happens when we're together, fostering creativity, collaboration, and connection. That's why we've adopted a hybrid approach, with teams in the office around four days a week. If you require accommodations or flexibility, please discuss this with the hiring team during the interview process. 

What does a Global Hub Operations Director do at WPP Production? 

Lead the operational performance and development of Studio A's global production hub network. The role sets a consistent operating standard across locations, turns demand into credible capacity plans, and ensures hubs can deliver secure, high quality work at the service levels and economics agreed with the client. It connects Hub Operations Leads, delivery and capability leaders, Geo teams, Commercial, Talent, HR, Finance, Technology and Facilities so that decisions on capacity, location, cost and risk are made with one view of the facts.

The Director leads through the Hub Operations Leads and the global operating cadence. They own the hub operating model and its execution, while partnering with the relevant functional and commercial owners on decisions outside hub operations.

Reporting lines and key stakeholders: 

- Reports to the Global Operations Director. Manages and develops the Hub Operations Leads across the global network, with clear local accountabilities and escalation routes.

- Covers centralised production hubs and the resources, infrastructure, controls and services required to support Worldwide and Geo demand, including permanent and flexible capacity.

- Works in a matrix with Heads of Delivery, capability SMEs, Geo and client operations, Commercial, Talent, HR, Finance, Security, Technology and Facilities. Local employment, technical craft and client commercial approval remain with their designated owners.

Key Responsibilities:

Global hub strategy and governance

- Set the hub operating model, decision rights and governance for shared capacity, including how Worldwide and Geo demand is prioritised, allocated and escalated when requirements conflict.

- Maintain a practical Hub Playbook covering planning, onboarding, access and security, local compliance, service management, financial controls, business continuity and location specific requirements. Audit adoption and close gaps.

- Assess the hub footprint against demand, capability, resilience, cost, security and talent availability. Develop business cases and transition plans for expansion, consolidation or changes in the mix of work across locations.

- Run a regular hub leadership cadence, with consistent status reporting, decisions, actions and cross hub learning. Chair operational reviews and escalate material trade offs promptly.

Capacity, workforce and delivery

- Translate demand forecasts, Workshop peaks and capability plans into a rolling view of capacity by hub, skill, language, security classification and employment type. Test scenarios for changes in volume, complexity, timing and location.

- Work with Delivery, SMEs and Geo leaders to allocate shared resources, manage utilisation and productivity, protect service levels and balance work across hubs. Identify bottlenecks early and agree actions rather than relying on local workarounds.

- Set requirements for permanent and flexible staffing with Talent and HR; oversee readiness, onboarding, training and exit planning for large scale programmes and demand changes. Ensure employment classification and local legal or tax questions go to the accountable specialists.

- Lead operational readiness for Workshops and other surges, including space, technology, security, access, staffing, shifts, supplier support and contingency capacity.

- Own the operational response to a hub disruption. Keep tested continuity and recovery plans, including transfer options, cross training, access dependencies and client approvals where required.

Commercial performance and controls

- Provide the operational data and discipline needed to run the commercial model as agreed: retained capacity, complexity based deliverables and approved time and materials exceptions. Ensure work is coded and measured consistently so actual demand, effort and cost can be compared with the model.

- Partner with Commercial and Finance on forecast accuracy, capacity pool economics, the minimum spend commitment, margin, scope changes, rush requests and Workshop demand. Identify the operational causes of variance and propose corrective actions; do not change prices or commitments without the agreed approval route.

- Supply a reliable monthly operational pack covering volumes and complexity, capacity and utilisation, forecast accuracy, service levels, quality, revisions and exceptions. Support quarterly commercial reviews of spend, margin, demand, savings and capacity risks, and the annual review of unit prices, cost adjustment, efficiency commitment and baseline capacity.

- Drive measurable productivity and the contracted efficiency commitment through improved planning, workflow, automation and location mix while protecting quality, security and sustainable capacity. Validate savings with Finance and avoid double counting.

- Ensure hub financial procedures, hiring controls, approved rates, procurement and contractor processes are followed. Surface non compliant practices and remediate them with the accountable teams.

Systems, data and improvement

- Define the operational requirements and adoption plan for the resource management platform, including estimates, staffing plans, scenario planning, schedules, timesheets, PTO and overtime, capacity reporting and relevant integrations.

- Set data definitions, ownership and quality controls across hubs so leadership can trust capacity, productivity, delivery and cost reporting. Use the data to diagnose recurring constraints and measure whether interventions work.

- Partner with Technology and process owners on rollout of production tools, language capacity planning, freelancer management and workflow improvements. Ensure local teams are trained and changes are embedded.

People, partnerships and risk

- Lead, coach and assess Hub Operations Leads. Build an integrated leadership team with clear expectations, succession cover and consistent management standards across locations.

- Build trusted relationships with senior Delivery, Geo, capability and client operations stakeholders. Make trade offs visible, resolve competing priorities and communicate decisions with clarity.

- Oversee hub risks relating to security, confidentiality, health and safety, infrastructure, service continuity and local compliance. Maintain a visible risk and action log, with owners and deadlines, and escalate issues that need executive decisions.

Measures of success

- Reliable delivery against agreed service levels, quality and security requirements across the hub network.

- Capacity and forecast accuracy by pool, with healthy utilisation, controlled overtime and a clear response to peaks and gaps.

- Commercial performance supported by trusted operational data, early variance management and validated efficiency gains.

- Consistent controls and operating standards, evidenced through reviews, audit actions and business continuity readiness.

- Effective Hub Operations Leads, clear stakeholder confidence and decisions made at the right level.

Requirements 

- Senior operations leadership in a complex, multi location production, agency, shared services or comparable environment, including management through local leaders and matrix teams.

- Strong command of capacity planning, workforce mix, service performance, financial controls and commercially consequential operational decisions.

- Ability to turn incomplete demand and cost data into practical scenarios, recommendations and executive decisions. Confident with metrics and able to challenge assumptions.

- Experience of scaling or reshaping hub operations, leading change in systems and processes, and managing security and continuity requirements.

- Direct, collaborative leadership; sound judgement under pressure; strong stakeholder management across cultures and functions; concise written and verbal communication.

This regional recruitment campaign is designed to build engineering capability closer to the customers and communities we support. Department Description

Allica Bank has won multiple recent Commercial Mortgage awards with the CM products being the main driver of lending in the Allica suite, the Commercial Mortgage products have now been well established for over 2 years and continue to grow at pace as a market leader. As part of the risk function within Commercial Mortgages, this role is critical to ensure we can deliver on our objectives in a safe manner.

Role Description

The purpose of the role is to underwrite borrowing requests received via a variety of channels, including online in line with the Bank’s approved Credit Policy and in accordance with the Banks asset portfolio (including but not limited to commercial mortgages, commercial investment loans, commercial loans against leasehold properties) .

Principle Accountabilities

- Assess and underwrite direct credit loan applications within personal discretion, in line with the all regulatory requirements, the Bank’s credit appetite policy and underwriting policies utilising appropriate credit data and analytical tools.

- Produce clear, accurate and concise written documentation, making clear recommendations to the Credit team for loan application requests falling outside of personal discretion or outside of credit policy, escalating cases where necessary to the appropriate Delegated Lending Authorities.

- Manage and own the end to end application process, from initial enquiry to completion, liaising effectively with the panel solicitors in terms of required security instructions and ensure loans are appropriately documented and borrowing is fully secured before draw-down.

- Liaise with the Credit team as required in managing the credit risk environment, concentration risk and developing credit policy.

- Undertake regular checks and monitor agreed controls to ensure the Bank’s risk and customer requirements are met at all times; escalating immediately any areas of concern

- Manage a portfolio of advances to a defined arrears and collections policy.

- Liaise effectively with applicants (or their brokers) and valuers in requests for additional relevant information to support the credit decisioning process.

- Deliver an excellent service is given to customers, their brokers and Relationship Managers, building and maintaining strong relationships in line with the Bank’s values and defined customer experience standards.

- Ensure compliance with all mandatory policies and adherence to credit procedures to maintain internal credit controls.

- Fully understand and comply with operational procedures, requirements and SLA’s.

- Help develop appropriate MI and KPI indicators and reporting, maintaining suitable MI to enable a detailed understanding of Mortgage processing pipeline

- Actively search for areas of improvement for the Bank and your team and take ownership for delivery of these, setting a good example by displaying appropriate values and behaviour

Personal Attributes & Experience

- Exposure/knowledge of underwriting, with experience in the SME sector, with an understanding of the competitor landscape and the dynamics and trends of the SME market.

- Excellent credit/financial analysis skills including the analysis of financial accounts, budgets and cashflow forecasting, Understanding of the loan underwriting process and the risks involved and be able to assess applications within a personal discretion and make recommendations and take commercial decisions.

- Experience of escalating and presenting at Credit Committee level and Arrears Management.

- Strong analytical, verbal and written communication skills.

- Ability to build strong and lasting relationships with internal stakeholders such as the distribution team, operations team and senior management, plus 3rd party suppliers such as Intermediaries, Valuers and Solicitors.

title: Applied AI - Member of Technical Staff
description:
About Us 

We’re living through a Cambrian explosion of intelligence: new models and new chips, each specialised for different tasks, are arriving all at once. The result is a new era for AI, one of radical heterogeneity.

Callosum is the Intelligent Systems Company. We believe the next generation of AI won't be defined by any single model or chip, but by intelligent systems in which hardware and intelligence co-evolve. We are building the infrastructure that unifies heterogeneous compute across the full stack. This opens a new axis of scaling intelligence: a dynamic system that tailors itself to what each workload actually needs, whether that's speed, cost, precision, or whatever unit comes next.

The last era scaled on a different bet: one bigger model, more of the same chip, more data. That bet is running into structural limits. Frontier models offer extraordinary capability at unsustainable cost, one that today's monolithic infrastructure was never designed to serve.

Our founding principle is that intelligence comes from many specialised systems working together, not from any single component. We build the software orchestration layer that co-evolves models, workflows and silicon into one system, delivering inference tailored to every workload, and demonstrating orders-of-magnitude leaps in capability and cost.

Because our software spans the full stack, our engineering team works directly with heterogeneous accelerators and frontier silicon, including Cerebras, d-Matrix, Intel, NVIDIA, AMD, Normal Computing, Tenstorrent, GreatSky, and Mixx. We are not stopping at today's chips: each new generation of silicon unlocks algorithms that couldn't run before, and we intend to be first to them, every time. If we get it right, it will belong to everyone building on it - not to any single vendor.

In our latest funding round, we raised $100M, led by Atomico with participation from Plural, DCVC and the UK Sovereign AI Fund’s first investment. With this, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of intelligence.

We are engineers and scientists based in London, working across the full depth of the stack. We are curious, intellectually honest, and building what doesn't exist yet. If you thrive on uncharted territory and are energised by the scale of the challenge, we'd love to hear from you.

About the Role 

The Applied AI team own Callosum's customer engagements end to end. You will work directly with customer engineering teams to understand their AI workloads, design and run rigorous evaluations against their production pipelines, integrate optimised workflows into their systems, and make sure the results hold in production.

At Callosum, Applied AI Engineers are the technical bridge between what customers run and what we build. What you learn shapes the research and platform roadmap. The evaluations you run are how we prove the technology in production. As an early member of the team, you will help build the methodology, tooling, and engagement practices the function runs on. The role is engineering-led: you will employ technical judgment to recognise what kind of system a problem needs and prototype it.

You will work closely with the engineers designing new intelligent systems, with the platform team that serves them, and directly with senior technical stakeholders on the customer side. We run a flat Member of Technical Staff structure. Responsibility and scope grow with what you demonstrate, including leadership of the Applied AI function as the team scales.

What You'll Build 

- Customer engagement from first workload scoping through evaluation, integration, and production deployment

- Design and run rigorous evaluations on customers' production workloads: set success criteria, instrument the comparison, present results to their engineering teams

- Develop deep technical understanding of customer systems (retrieval pipelines, agentic workflows, code intelligence stacks) and design optimised Callosum workflows

- Integrate Callosum workflows into customer environments and support them through to stable production

- Work with our research and platform teams to turn what you learn into general product capability

- Build the team's shared methodology: evaluation harnesses, integration runbooks, and engagement standards

What You Bring 

- Exceptional technical depth, demonstrated through any of: production systems at scale, research that shipped, or an early/founding role where you owned the system end to end

- Experience with LLM serving infrastructure, agent orchestration, or retrieval systems

- Rigour in evaluation or benchmarking work 

- A bias for action, comfort with ambiguity and a strong sense of ownership

What Sets You Apart 

- Experience working directly with external engineering teams, whether as a forward deployed engineer, solutions architect, technical consultant, or comparable customer-facing role

- Familiarity with novel accelerator platforms

- Experience at an early-stage company or in a founding-engineer role

What We Offer

- Competitive Salary, determined by skills and experience

- Equity & Ownership

- Private healthcare

- We offer Visa sponsorship and relocation benefits to hire the best in the world

- We work in person at our London office. You'll have the tools, space and setup to do your best work, and if you have specific needs, just tell us

About Freetrade

Freetrade’s mission is to become the default place to invest. Investing has been too complicated and expensive for too long, keeping millions from making the most of their savings.

We’re changing that.

We’re building our team and looking for people who are excited to reshape how our customers invest and grow their wealth. If you’re driven by solving complex problems and building innovative products, you’ll fit right in.

2026 is a big year for us. Last year, we announced a game changing deal to become part of the IG Group. We’ll continue to operate as an independent business while gaining access to the resources and support of an established leader in the space.

This year, we’re accelerating our roadmap and taking our products to the next level. We’re building new features like mutual funds, bonds, and family investment tools. We’re also exploring how we can leverage AI to deliver an even better experience for our customers.

About the role 

As part of IG Group, Freetrade combines the pace of a scale-up with the backing of a global leader in trading. We're now looking for a Head of Security, Privacy & IT to lead us into our next phase of growth. Millions of people trust us with billions of pounds in assets, and you'll lead the team that keeps them safe. You'll drive the roadmap, make the calls and stay close enough to the technical work to shape it directly. As we launch new products, you'll make sure we move quickly and safely, and lead how we adopt AI securely across the company. Working closely with Risk, People and Legal, you'll build a world-class security and privacy by design culture.

What you'll do 

Leadership 

- Lead a high-calibre team across security, privacy and IT, setting clear priorities and developing the people in it

- Create the roadmap and turn it into delivery, balancing risk reduction with the pace the business needs

- Advise the leadership team on security and privacy risk, with clear, pragmatic recommendations they can act on

- Set the guardrails for AI across Freetrade, from employee tooling to AI features in our products, so teams can adopt it with confidence

- Represent Freetrade within IG Group's security community, sharing what works and bringing in best practice

Security 

- Own application and cloud security, building security into the SDLC so engineers catch issues early

- Get hands-on in the design of new products and evolving our services

- Own incident detection and response, from 24/7 monitoring to running the response when it matters

- Secure how we use AI in practice, , including native integrations and MCP,

- Drive a culture of security awareness and embedding security by design principles across Freetrade

Privacy 

- Ensure UK/EU GDPR compliance as the company scales

- Act as first line of defense on GDPR across vendor review, onboarding, and engineering/data changes

- Report regularly to senior leadership on privacy posture

- Handle DSRs from users and employees, and liaise with regulators when required

- Govern privacy-by-design adoption of AI

IT 

- Own corporate IT and workplace technology across London and Budapest

- Ensure secure site and remote connectivity (network, VPN/ZTNA) across both office sites

- Ensure smooth management for the full employee technology lifecycle: onboarding, offboarding, and role changes, including hardware provisioning and access provisioning/deprovisioning

- Own identity and access management: SSO, directory services, access reviews, and joiner-mover-leaver processes

- Own corporate infrastructure, hardware fleet, and software tooling (procurement, licensing, lifecycle management)

About you 

- 8+ years in the tech industry

- 3+ years of people management experience, managing a team of similar size

- Solid understanding of GDPR core principles and expectations

- Experience managing multiple functions or a diverse remit is a plus

- Fintech or regulated industry experience is a plus

- IT/workplace tech experience is a plus

Our hybrid model

title: Senior Data Analyst – Labour & Productivity
description:

We are currently selecting an advanced scheduling platform to support this. The analytical foundation underneath it,how we measure productivity, what our labour standards are, how good our demand forecasts need to be - is what this role owns.

You will sit in the Data team and work in close partnership with FP&A. Analysis alone will not move the number; changes stick when a Finance Business Partner and a General Manager can see the opportunity in their own House, agree the size of it and hold it in their forecast. Your job is to give them that, in a form they can act on.

Key Responsibilities.. 

- Labour productivity analysis, identifying site-by-site opportunities for efficiency gains and sizing each one

- Work with Operations and Finance to trial changes to scheduling and measure their impact

- Build improved labour reporting, so Business Partners and GMs can see productivity, schedule changes and shift adherence on a daily and weekly cadence

- Support Finance translate demand forecasts into labour requirements, helping to build the models that turn covers, check-ins, treatments and occupancy into hours by role

- Partner with our Data Science and Operations teams to understand forecast accuracy and recommend improvements

- Connect labour deployment to member experience, so that productivity gains are demonstrably not coming out of the House

What we are looking for.. 

- Proven experience in labour optimisation. You have personally delivered measurable improvement in wage percentage or sales per labour hour in a multi-site operation, and can talk us through the levers you pulled, how you sized them and how you proved the result

- A track record of partnering finance and operational stakeholders to land change, not just report on it

- Several years in an analytics role, with genuine multi-site operational exposure — hospitality, retail, leisure or QSR

- Advanced SQL, and comfort in a modelled data warehouse (experience with dbt an advantage)

- BI development experience (Omni, Looker, Tableau or Power BI), building tools operators actually use

- Experience with rota, time and attendance and payroll data, and a realistic view of its challenges

- Able to evaluate a demand forecast critically — accuracy, bias, seasonality — without needing to build one

Desirable.. 

- Experience with a workforce management or scheduling platform — Unifocus, HotSchedules, Dayforce, Fourth, S4 Labour, UKG, Quinyx or similar

- Strong financial modelling and fluency in P&L mechanics — wage percentage, flow-through, contribution

- An understanding of how labour regulation constrains labour models internationally, particularly the US — predictive scheduling and fair workweek rules, overtime and break requirements

- Labour standards or time-and-motion experience

- Python for data analysis and modelling, and/or use of AI tooling such as Claude Code to accelerate it

- Experience linking labour deployment to customer experience outcomes

- Une architecture distribuée et scalable conçue pour traiter en temps réel les flux de la plateforme 

- Une plateforme modulaire soumise à des contraintes de haute disponibilité et de sécurisation des données, capable de gérer de fortes audience 

Contexte 
L'offre de paris sportifs chez Winamax repose sur le traitement en temps réel de flux massifs de données et l'ajustement continu de probabilités. Pour garantir la cohérence entre les cotes et l'exposition financière de Winamax, l'analyse automatisée des mouvements de marché, du volume des mises et des activités atypiques est devenue un enjeu stratégique.

La question à laquelle doit répondre le stage : 
Comment détecter algorithmiquement les incohérences de probabilités et les volumes atypiques en temps réel pour fournir un Indice de Confiance fiable, capable d'assister la prise de décision ?

Objectifs du stage 

- Modéliser la cohérence des cotes et un Indice de Confiance : Concevoir des modèles statistiques pour repérer les décalages de probabilités et évaluer en temps réel la fiabilité des activités à fort volume, en croisant la notoriété de l'événement et son historique

- Intégrer le module au cœur de l'outil trading existant : Développer une brique algorithmique performante qui s'interface directement avec l'application métier des traders, afin d'enrichir leurs outils

- Validation & mesure de performance (Backtesting) : Tester et calibrer les modèles sur des historiques massifs de données pour maximiser leur précision, minimiser les fausses alertes et mesurer l'impact réel de l'outil sur l'activité

Les points d'attention 

- Temps réel et faible latence : capacité à traiter des flux à haute fréquence (milliers d'actualisations et d'activités par seconde) sans ralentir la réactivité des outils

- Volume de données et backtesting : manipulation de séries temporelles complexes et capacité à tester/ajuster les modèles sur des bases historiques de plusieurs millions de lignes

- Précision du ciblage (taux de faux positifs) : nécessité d'ajuster finement les seuils statistiques pour remonter des signaux réellement pertinents sans engorger l'outil d'alertes inutiles
